sections.heading: Selling Directly From a Mechanic Shop or Body Shop (Avoiding the Storage Fee Trap)
sections.body:
Here is one of the most common scenarios in auto salvaging: Your car overheats or loses drive power on the highway, so you have it towed to a local mechanic or dealership. The shop charges a $150 diagnostic fee and calls you the next afternoon with terrible news—you need a $5,500 replacement engine or a $4,200 transmission rebuild on a car worth $3,000.

When you decline the repair, a ticking financial clock starts immediately:

  • Daily Shop Storage Fees ($35–$100/Day): Almost every repair work order you sign when dropping off your keys includes fine print allowing the shop to charge daily storage fees starting 24 to 48 hours after you decline an estimate. Within ten days, a $50/day storage bill equals $500—wiping out the scrap value of your car.
  • Diagnostic Bill vs. Mechanic's Lien: Under state ”garageman's lien” laws, a repair shop has the legal right to retain physical possession of your vehicle until your authorized diagnostic or teardown bill is paid. However, if you call the service writer and say, “I'm not fixing the car, I'm having USJunkCars pick it up tomorrow—how much do I owe for the diagnostic so you'll release the keys?”, nine times out of ten the mechanic will happily waive storage fees (and sometimes even discount the diagnostic fee) just to get a dead car out of their valuable bay or crowded parking lot!

How Mechanic Shop Pickups Work Step-by-Step:

  1. Get Your Instant Offer: Enter your VIN and the mechanic shop's ZIP code on our home page to lock in your guaranteed cash offer.
  2. Clear Your Balance With the Shop: Call the mechanic, pay any small diagnostic fee over the phone by card, and tell the service manager that our tow partner will be picking up the car.
  3. Meet the Driver or Arrange a Shop Drop-Off: You can either meet our tow driver at the repair shop for 10 minutes to hand over the signed title and collect your check on the spot, or if you are stuck at work, you can leave the properly signed title in an envelope with the shop's front desk and our dispatcher can arrange payment pickup/delivery according to state verification rules. (If you lost your title, check our guide on how to sell a junk car without a title first).

Once the tow truck picks up your vehicle from the shop, remember to follow our post-sale license plate and DMV release of liability guide—ask the mechanic to unscrew your plates and hold them at the front counter for you if you won't be at the shop during pickup!

sections.heading: Frequently Asked Questions (People Also Ask)
sections.body:
Can a tow truck get a junk car out of a tight parallel street parking spot?

Yes. Even if your dead car is parallel-parked on a narrow city street with cars parked bumper-to-bumper in front and behind it, a wheel-lift tow truck can still extract it. Wheel-lift operators use an angled ”pivot snatch” technique with wheel dollies/skates to slide the front or rear end of your car out into the traffic lane at a 45-degree angle without touching the bumpers of neighboring cars. Just let our dispatcher know it is boxed in on a street so we send a wheel-lift truck rather than a long rollback flatbed.

Can USJunkCars pay the mechanic shop my unpaid diagnostic bill and give me the difference?

For legal and accounting reasons, salvage buyers must issue the full purchase payment directly to the legal owner listed on the vehicle title, rather than splitting checks with a third-party repair shop. However, if you meet our driver at the mechanic shop, our driver hands you your guaranteed payment on the spot—and you can walk right inside the shop lobby to pay your diagnostic invoice and walk away with the remaining profit in your pocket.

Do I have to be physically present when the tow truck picks up my junk car?

In most cases, having the owner (or a designated friend, spouse, or family member over 18) present for 5 to 10 minutes is the fastest way to hand over the signed title, show photo ID, and receive your on-the-spot payment. However, if your car is at a mechanic shop or apartment lot and your work schedule makes meeting impossible, contact our dispatch team—in many service locations, we can verify your ID and title remotely so you can leave the keys and title with the mechanic shop's front desk or a lockbox.

What if my car is in pieces at the mechanic shop after an engine teardown?

We buy disassembled and partially torn-down vehicles every day! Just instruct the mechanic to place all removed engine components, intake manifolds, bolts, and the catalytic converter inside the trunk or back seat so the vehicle's complete weight and core parts remain intact, and let us know the drivetrain is disassembled when getting your quote. Visit our FAQ page for more details on how vehicle condition affects your offer.
